a1
Rachel had no children, and she envied her sister Leah. She told Jacob: give me children, or I will die.
a2
Jacob answered: am I God, who has kept children from you?
b1
Rachel and Leah each gave Jacob a maid. The maids bore four sons: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
b2
Leah bore two more sons, Issachar and Zebulun, and a daughter, Dinah.
c1
Then God remembered Rachel. She bore a son and said: God has taken away my shame. She named him Joseph.
d1
Jacob asked Laban: let me go home with my wives and children. Laban said: I have learned the Lord blessed me because of you. Name your wages.
d2
Jacob asked for the dark lambs and the spotted goats as his wages. Laban agreed, then sent those animals three days away.
e1
Still, Jacob's flocks grew, and he became very rich, with servants, camels, and donkeys.
h1
Rachel longed for a child, and she compared herself to her sister.
h2
In the middle of the rivalry, the text says: God remembered Rachel.
h3
Waiting is not being forgotten. Comparison makes the wait heavier.
h4
Today, bring your waiting to God, and let go of the count.
i
Whose life are you comparing yourself to?
